text.p: U.S. Diagnostic Inc said Wednesday it had agreed in principle to acquire American Shared Hospital Services in a stock swap.
U.S. Diagnostic said it would issue $2.40 of stock for each outstanding share of American Shared.
American Shared has about 4.75 million outstanding shares and 2.22 million outstanding options and warrants.
American Shared announced the deal on December 11, 1996.
The agreement in principle is subject to, among other things, execution of a definitive merger agreement, expected shortly, and approval by American Shared shareholders.
The deal is expected to close within 90 days, U.S. Diagnostic said.
U.S. Diagnostic Chairman and Chief Executive Jeffrey Goffman said in a statement that the pooling of interests is accretive and allows the company to use its common stock and avoid goodwill charges.
The president of U.S. Diagnostic, Joseph Paul, said one factor that made the deal possible was the signing of a letter of intent with General Electric Co to restructure American Shared's debt.
"We are also working with GE on a potential joint venture to have them provide nationwide maintenance service for U.S. Diagnostic equipment," Paul said.

U.S. Diagnostic provides radiology services focused on the acquisition, operation and management of multi-modality diagnostic imaging centers and related medical facilities in the U.S. American Shared owns 32 MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) magnets, as well as CT, ultrasound and other diagnostic imaging equipment. It provides mobile imaging services in 22 states.
